decision_rationale: Both installed simulator repositories were located, inspected, and had concrete build/execution attempted (not merely assumed blocked). Accel-Sim: in-tree build failed on pre-existing root-owned directories (no sudo); worked around via an Expansion-relocated source copy; standalone nvcc compilation then confirmed FUNDAMENTALLY BROKEN on this host via a minimal, torch-free, project-free reproduction (CUDA 13.1 vs this glibc/GCC-15.2 'rsqrt' header conflict) -- a genuine SIMULATOR_INCOMPATIBILITY, not an unattempted approval gate. gem5: build launched successfully (scons installed via pip, build-dir relocated to Expansion, resource-monitored via /usr/bin/time -v, peak RSS only ~324MB, no OOM), failed fast on a missing m4 dependency; a concrete user-local source-build workaround for m4 was attempted and itself failed on an independent, diagnosed gnulib/GCC-15.2 incompatibility. Neither track produced real SIMULATOR_OUTPUT evidence. Meanwhile, the evidence taxonomy and claim gate (Phase 1/2) are fully implemented, tested (21/21 new tests), and demonstrated against real E2E-11 hardware data: three claims promoted (PROMOTE_HARDWARE_VALIDATED) and one aggregate claim correctly downgraded using real measured numbers. No existing three-family behavior regressed (1958 total tests passing). This matches PROVENANCE_GATE_SUCCESS_SIMULATION_INCONCLUSIVE precisely: the gate/provenance side succeeded; the simulation side is inconclusive due to concretely-diagnosed toolchain incompatibilities on this specific host, not due to skipped effort.

resource_conclusion.existing_swap_sufficient: yes (never approached; swap usage did not increase during any attempted build)
resource_conclusion.peak_rss_m4_build_attempt: not separately captured via /usr/bin/time -v (small, fast build attempt); no memory pressure observed via free -h before/after
